source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Wait for senior administration to solve the problem because entry-level RNs do not participate in quality-improvement work involving client outcomes.","B":"Change the fall-prevention policy independently and immediately because an individual nurse should bypass the unit's improvement process when outcome data worsen.","C":"Participate in the structured improvement process by reviewing the data and evidence, helping test appropriate changes, and evaluating their effect on client outcomes.","D":"Stop reporting falls until a new prevention strategy is selected because reducing the number of incident reports will make the unit's performance data more accurate."}}
source_row.rationale: NCSBN explicitly includes participation in performance-improvement projects and quality-improvement processes, use of research, and evaluation of improvement measures under Management of Care. Option C matches the entry-level RN role. Option A incorrectly excludes staff nurses. Option B bypasses the organized process and policy governance. Option D corrupts safety data rather than improving care.
source_row.source_detail: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan — Management of Care, Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22: define PI/quality-assurance activities; participate in PI projects and QI processes; utilize research/references; evaluate the impact of PI measures on client care and resource use. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; official NCSBN/NCLEX source currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: continuity/transfer of care, collaboration, legal/regulatory scope, quality improvement, leadership and professional-practice activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A unit's fall rate has increased for three consecutive months. Which action by the staff nurse best reflects the RN's role in performance improvement?
